text:
maria_g: Heads up — trying to onboard a HF model that uses a custom config + trust_remote_code. Redwood convert fails and chat templates are garbling special tokens. Anyone seen this?
rahul: which model id? error logs?
maria_g: model: hf-acme/gptx-7b-custom. Convert command: `redwood convert hf-acme/gptx-7b-custom --out /tmp/gptx-converted`
maria_g: failure output: 
```
ERROR: auto_map resolution for class 'CustomModelConfig' not found
tokenizer special_tokens_map missing: expected '<|sep|>' but found '<|sep>'
Traceback: KeyError: 'eos_token'
```
olivia: ugh classic trust_remote_code pain. HF has a custom config class that defines tokenizer attrs differently. Did you enable `--trust-remote-code`?
maria_g: I tried both. `--trust-remote-code` makes conversion proceed but tokenizer mapping still wrong. Chat template injection uses '<|sep|>' but tokenizer file has '<|sep>' (missing pipe).
ben_k: that mismatch will break prefix/KV-cache alignment. Also saw weird token id shifts after quantize -> massive eval drift on FRQA bench.
rahul: quick check: open the original `config.json` and `tokenizer_config.json` from the repo. Often `tokenizer_class` or `special_tokens_map` keys are custom-named. Can you paste both small snippets?
maria_g: pasted relevant bits: 
```
// from config.json
"architectures": ["CustomModel"],
"custom_attr": true,
"tokenizer_type": "acme_tokenizer_v2"
// tokenizer_config.json
"special_tokens": {"sep_token": "<|sep>", "eos_token": "<|end|>"}
```
olivia: right there — they renamed `sep_token` value and used a different key name `special_tokens`. Our HF-to-Redwood conversion expects `eos_token`, `bos_token`, `sep_token` at top-level or in `tokenizer.json` mapping. Auto_map usually handles it but only if `trust_remote_code` exposes the custom tokenizer class that knows the mapping.
rahul: two approaches: 1) patch the repo before conversion (add a `special_tokens_map.json` with canonical keys), or 2) use `--trust-remote-code` + provide an override mapping file `--token-mapping overrides.json` (we have a helper in infra).
maria_g: tried patching `special_tokens_map.json` and re-running — convert succeeded but chat template still prints literal token markers in responses (so decode mismatch). Example: model output: "Hello<|sep|> how can I help" instead of a space+separator token being consumed.
ben_k: sounds like the tokenizer's internal `added_tokens` table maps the token string to a different id than expected. When we quantize later (int8), the id ordering changed and eval BLEU/QA metrics dropped ~6 points on our smoke tests. I have logs: 
```
quantize.log: mapping table len=8
original ids: [50256, 11, 50257]
post-quant ids: [50257, 50256, 11]
```
ben_k: that's consistent with the tokenizer being rebuilt during conversion.
olivia: also check chat template JSON: some HF repos include `chat_template.json` that uses raw token strings. We should normalize templates to use special token placeholders like `{sep_token}`.
rahul: actionable steps: 1) dump tokenizer.encodings before/after conversion: `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('path').get_vocab()[:20])"` 2) run conversion with `--trust-remote-code` and `--dump-mapping mmap.json` 3) run decode test with `tokenizer.decode([ids])` to assert separators decode correctly.
maria_g: running step 2 now, CI job created: ci-bot started conversion job #342 (artifact at s3://infra-test/gptx/342)
ci-bot: conversion job 342 queued by maria_g. logs: https://ci.redwood/gptx/342/logs
maria_g: update — dump shows tokenizer vocab contains both `'<|sep>'` and `'<|sep|>'` as separate tokens. That's the root cause. Repo had legacy and new tokens.
olivia: oh interesting — double tokens. Need to merge mappings: prefer the pipe-inclusive token and remap the legacy id to it, update chat templates.
ben_k: warning — remapping token ids post-quant will change shape of embedding matrix if not handled. Best to remap pre-quant and re-align embeddings: run `scripts/remap_tokens.py --from old.json --to canonical.json` then quantize.
rahul: for now, quick fix for staging: create a small shim tokenizer wrapper where `decode` rewrites legacy token string -> canonical and `encode` substitutes canonical tokens. Ugly but fast.
maria_g: shim worked, chat renders correct. Tests pass locally. But benchmark numbers still slightly worse after int8: latency fine, but qa_f1 dropped 4 pts. Might be quantization/regression unrelated to tokens.
ben_k: can you run eval with FP16 model (no quant) to isolate? If FP16 matches baseline then it's quant. If FP16 already degraded then tokenizer change introduced numeric differences during tokenization/positioning.
maria_g: FP16 run scheduled. One more gotcha: the model's `auto_map` in `config.json` points to a remote class path that differs from the pip-package name. That caused our auto_map resolver to skip the HF loader and fallback to generic base class. We should log that as a warning in converter.
olivia: agreed — filed infra ticket INFRA-1298 to add warning + a `--force-remote-class` flag. @rahul can you pick up?
rahul: yep, will add forced resolver and a small validation step that checks `special_tokens` normalized.
ci-bot: INFRA-1298 created by olivia. Link: https://tracker.redwood/INFRA-1298
maria_g: thanks — will patch repo (merge special tokens, add canonical special_tokens_map.json) and re-run with your forced-resolver once available.
ben_k: also add a regression eval job to the conversion pipeline — run QA/SMOKE and FRQA after conversion+quant to catch these quickly.
maria_g: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
